title: Microsoft Purview DLP: guided diagnostics for why a policy acted
summary: The rollout details and both published navigation paths are supported. Hold because the briefing treats Security Copilot consumption and platform-wide data controls as unconfirmed despite documentation covering embedded experiences, understates the cost model, and presents a personal plugin toggle as tenant-wide.

claims.quote: We’re introducing a new guided diagnostics experience to help users understand why their DLP policies may not be behaving as expected.

claims.claim: The notice does not define the roles that confer permission to view DLP policies.
claims.quote: The diagnostics will be available to all users who have permission to view DLP policies.

claims.claim: Rules execute in priority order within each DLP policy.
claims.quote: A policy contains one or more rules. Rules are executed sequentially, starting with the highest-priority rule in each policy.

claims.claim: For hosted locations such as Exchange, SharePoint and OneDrive, the first evaluated matching rule with the most restrictive action is enforced.
claims.quote: For the hosted service locations, like Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive ... If content matches multiple rules, the first rule evaluated that has the most restrictive action is enforced.

claims.claim: Security Copilot may copy, process and store relevant Customer Data to provide responses.
claims.quote: Relevant Customer Data may be copied, processed, and stored by Security Copilot to provide responses.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not said whether Security Copilot's documented data processing applies to the DLP insights.
claims.quote: Microsoft Security products purchased by you may share data, including Customer Data, as described in the product documentation. Customer Data shared with Security Copilot is governed by the Product Terms, Data Protection Addendum, and documentation applicable to Security Copilot.
claims.fix: Replace the uncertainty sentence with: 'Data shared with Security Copilot is governed by Security Copilot product terms, data protection commitments and documentation; the notice identifies existing DLP configuration data and diagnostic metadata as inputs.' Keep the narrower statement that the notice introduces no new customer content sources.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 services data access defaults to ON when Security Copilot is auto-provisioned for E5 or E7.
claims.quote: Accessing data from Microsoft 365 services ... By default, this setting is set to ON.

claims.claim: Managing Owner settings requires the Security Copilot owner role.
claims.quote: You need the Security Copilot owner role to manage owner settings.

claims.claim: Security Copilot in Purview is enabled by default.
claims.quote: Security Copilot in Purview is enabled by default.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 services data access is configured in the Security Copilot portal under Settings > Owner settings.
claims.quote: Configuring Microsoft 365 services data access ... In Security Copilot, go to Settings > Owner settings.
claims.fix: Keep the cited path, but add: 'Microsoft documentation also describes Owner > Owner settings in the home menu; see https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/security/navigating-security-copilot#use-the-home-menu.' That page lists Owner settings under Owner and describes Settings as theme, time zone and language preferences.

claims.claim: The Purview source toggle is reached through Security Copilot portal > Sources > Manage plugins > Purview.
claims.quote: Open Sources in the prompt bar. ... On the Manage plugins page, set the Purview toggle to On to enable or Off to disable.

claims.claim: No dedicated UI switch or automation control for enabling, disabling or restricting the new guided diagnostics is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "guided diagnostics" "DLP" "tenant" disable PowerShell; Purview "guided diagnostics" PowerShell licensing permission switch. Read MC1293479, DLP policy reference and Test your DLP policies; no dedicated availability switch or API found.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for Security Copilot Microsoft 365 services data access is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Security Copilot" "Microsoft 365" "data access" "REST"; "Security Copilot" "owner settings" "PowerShell" "Graph". Opened Privacy and data security, Owner settings and Auto provisioning; found UI instructions but no corresponding command or endpoint.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for the Security Copilot Purview plugin toggle is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Security Copilot" "Purview" "plugin" "API" enable disable; "Security Copilot" "plugins" "REST API" settings. Opened Copilot in Purview Overview, Manage plugins and Use plugins; no corresponding management command or endpoint found.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 services data access setting controls Security Copilot queries to services such as Purview.
claims.quote: This setting allows customers to configure whether Security Copilot can query information directly from Microsoft 365 services such as Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed whether disabling Microsoft 365 data access governs the DLP Security Copilot insights.
claims.quote: Customers can choose not to share their Microsoft 365 service data with Copilot in the Owner settings page. However, the organization won't be able to use Copilot with Microsoft 365 products such as like Microsoft Purview.
claims.fix: Replace the unconfirmed-applicability statements for row 2 with: 'The Microsoft 365 services data access setting governs Security Copilot integration with Purview; disabling it prevents the organisation from using Copilot with Purview.' Cite the already-listed Security Copilot inclusion page. Remove the corresponding open question about whether this setting removes the insights.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed whether the Purview source toggle governs the DLP Security Copilot insights.
claims.quote: Security Copilot in Purview must be enabled for both the standalone and embedded experiences to work.
claims.fix: Replace the unconfirmed-applicability statements for row 3 with: 'Microsoft documents the Purview source as required for both standalone and embedded Security Copilot experiences in Purview.' Remove the corresponding open question and the condition 'if Microsoft confirms they apply' from the checklist.

claims.claim: The Sources > Manage plugins > Purview toggle is a tenant-wide control.
claims.quote: To personalize the way Security Copilot interacts with you ... Turn any plugin on or off ... Select which plugins Security Copilot uses as a data source by turning service toggles on or off.
claims.fix: Change controls[2].scope and the rendered scope from tenant to user. Add to its note: 'This source toggle personalises the user's active plugins; it is not the organisation-wide plugin availability restriction.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/security/use-plugins for the distinction.

claims.claim: Security Copilot compute is measured in Security Compute Units.
claims.quote: A Security Compute Unit is a unit measure of the compute power to run Security Copilot workloads for AI capabilities within the standalone and embedded experiences.

claims.claim: E5 and E7 inclusion provides 400 SCUs per month for every 1,000 paid user licences.
claims.quote: Customers with Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 will have 400 Security Compute Units (SCU) each month for every 1,000 paid user license

claims.claim: The included monthly capacity is capped at 10,000 SCUs.
claims.quote: up to 10,000 SCUs each month

claims.claim: The included E5 and E7 SCU allocation has no additional cost.
claims.quote: up to 10,000 SCUs each month at no additional cost.

claims.claim: The cited inclusion page says usage beyond allocated SCUs will be throttled at a future date.
claims.quote: Usage beyond the allocated SCUs will be throttled at a future date.

claims.claim: At that future point, customers can scale beyond inclusion at $6 USD per SCU on a pay-as-you-go basis.
claims.quote: Customers have an option to scale beyond the allocated amount at $6 USD for each SCU on a pay-as-you go basis at that time.

claims.claim: Customers without E5 or E7 can continue using Security Copilot under its existing pricing model.
claims.quote: Customers without Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 licenses can continue to access Security Copilot using the existing pricing model.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Test-DlpPolicies is an existing item-level test for policies scoped to SharePoint and OneDrive, rather than a control over the new experience.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The guided diagnostics default state is on for their intended audience, without administrator enablement.
claims.quote: The diagnostics will be available to all users who have permission to view DLP policies. ... No action is required.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining licence eligibility with Security Copilot capacity.
claims.quote: Customers with Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 will have 400 Security Compute Units (SCU) each month for every 1,000 paid user license, up to 10,000 SCUs each month at no additional cost.

claims.claim: Cost is low because admin time is the only certain cost and SCU consumption is unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Briefing: 'Admin time is the only certain cost' and 'whether ... insights draw on Security Compute Units is not yet published.' Source: 'You consume SCUs ... Running embedded Security Copilot experiences'. The standard defines variable as metered.
claims.fix: Set cost to 'variable'. Replace the cost rationale with: 'Variable. Security Copilot-powered insights consume Security Compute Units, including allocated E5 capacity; a rate specific to these diagnostics is not yet published. Admin time is an additional indirect cost, and no licence specific to the base diagnostics is published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/security/security-compute-units-capacity.
